title.narrative: Rio Grande do Norte: Regional Development and Governance

description.narrative: The objective of the Project is to support the Borrower's efforts to: (i) increase food security, access to productive infrastructure and markets for family agriculture; (ii) improve the quality of, and access to, health, education and public security services; and (iii) improve systems for public expenditure, human resource and physical asset management in the context of a results-based management approach.

The objective of the Rio Grande do Norte Regional Development and Governance Project for Brazil is to support the borrower's efforts to: (i) increase food security and access to productive infrastructure and markets for family agriculture; (ii) improve the quality of, and access to, health, education and public security services; and (iii) improve systems for public expenditure, human resource and physical asset management in the context of a results-based management approach. The project has three components. (1) Sustainable regional development component will reduce regional inequalities and increase productive inclusion. (2) Improving public services component will support the human development and citizen security pillars of the state's poverty reduction strategy by improving the quality of, and access to, basic public services. (3) Public sector management component will provide support for the modernization of the state's public sector management in strategic sectors in order to strengthen the efficiency and effectiveness of central budget, finance and planning processes and management, as well as in service delivery in health, education and public security sectors.

Finance Agreement :Project Management Unit | Description :Loan Agreement - Schedule 2 Section I.A.2.(a) Operate and maintain,until the completion of the Project, a unit within SEPLAN (the PMU), responsible for the overall management, coordination,supervision, monitoring and evaluation of the Project. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Project Management Committee | Description :Loan Agreement - Schedule 2 Section I.A.1. No later than thirty daysafter the Effective Date, the Borrower shall establish, and thereafter operate and maintain during the implementation of theProject, a Project Management Committee chaired by SEPLAN's Secretary, and composed by representatives from key secretariats andorganizations. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Project Sectoral Units | Description :Loan Agreement - Schedule 2 Section I.A.2. (b) Operate and maintain, untilthe completion of the Project, sectoral units (the UES) within SAPE, SETHAS, SESAP, SESED, SEDEC, SEEC, SEARH, SETUR and DERresponsible for the management, and implementation, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of Project activities within theirrespective sectors | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

comment.narrative: Achieved 106% of a reduced target. Direct beneficiaries count all members of a beneficiary family for specified Component 1 investments, as envisaged. The project MIS recorded a single beneficiary per family which is multiplied by 3.4, IBGE average size of a rural household in the NE region. Women's participation counts female members of direct beneficiary households including female-headed households. The basis for counting beneficiaries is explained in footnote 26 Main Text and as intended after the 2019 restructuring, covers only specific investments under Component 1 because their regular measurement was simpler. The original PAD measurement concept was discarded. The BCR (2024) estimated total beneficiaries for major project activities (all Components). See Table xx ICR Annex 7.

Achieved 100% of target. Indicator intended to accompany and monitor implementation of public management systems installed with project support. Two systems implemented: (i) Financial and Budget Administration System of RN (SIGEF); (ii) Integrated Solution for Analytical Information and Mining of Data for RN State Administration. These 2 systems support 3 Objective Outcomes: Expenditures, Assets Management, and Human Resources Management. See Section IIB Main Text.

Exceeded: Achieved 634% of target. Refers to the number of socio-economic infrastructure implemented and includes: 178 Productive Infrastructure investments (see Table 2, Annex 7) and 139 larger scale social investments. In aggregate, the total includes: 9 roads; 18 tourist sites; 46 schools renovated/constructed; 21 Maternity units; Mossoro Women's Hospital; 7 Emergency Rooms; Cytopathology Laboratory (LAPAT/RN); 22 Citizen Services Centers; 5 Cancer Referral Units (CROS); 2 fiscal posts; 5 water supply and sanitation structures; 2 water sewage systems; Lucrecia Dam; DIBA Irrigation Scheme/Amorim Canal; Technology Park; and renovated State Administrative Center.

title.narrative: People benefited by subprojects promoting food security

comment.narrative: Achieved 112% of target. Description: Subprojects linked to food security were oriented to promoting access to water for production of healthy foods and guaranteeing safe and nutritional food for beneficiaries through use of cement-lined cisterns and systems for water re-use, enabling more viable productive plots, in subprojects under Call for Proposals #1, and the anti-desertification pilot subprojects; and (b) production of irrigated food crops and fruits. Introduced by 2nd restructuring in May 2019 and started to be reported in late 2019. Measurement: Beneficiaries are counted according to how their subprojects functioned: A/B x 100. A. Persons benefited by productive SPs and hydro-environmental works under Edital #1/2014 and who already concluded works/investments; and B. Total persons benefited by SPs linked to the promotion of food security. See details of Editais Footnote xx, Section II B, Main Text.

title.narrative: People assisted locally (municipal level) by preventive public security activities financed by the project

comment.narrative: Achieved 121.5% of target Preventative activities considered for measurement include: ITEP (identity cards, biometric kits); Civil Police (expanded vehicle fleet, digitalization of crime event registry); CIOSP (modernization, expansion of radio-communications system/network); and CODIMM (restructuring of facilities to attend women in violence situations; itinerant cinema/training, and Hotline Call-in for women).

title.narrative: Decrease in dropout rates of the state's secondary schools benefiting from the project

comment.narrative: Not achieved: 49% of target. The baseline was 12.3%, the target was 8% - an expected 4.3 pp reduction - and the project achieved 10.2%, or a 2.1% reduction (49% of target). Indicator calculated as ratio between no. students in state school system who abandon ensino medio/total no. students who enroll in this level in the state system at the start of school year. Project's potential to reduce dropout rates is seen in 9% result for 2019 vs target 8%. No data collected for 2020 - pandemic year with schools closed. Dropout rate declined in 2022 and 2023. This indicator was elevated from intermediate level at appraisal/PAD to PDO level in 2017.

title.narrative: Provision of health services related to prioritized health care networks at the regional level (maternal and infant, urgency and emergency, and oncological health care networks)

comment.narrative: Achieved only 18% of the expected 7.36 percentage point increase (baseline 76.64%, target 84%, result 78% = difference of 1.36%, or 18% of target) Sources include the Outpatient Information System of the Unified Health System (SIA/SUS), the Hospital Information System (SIH) and est. of population by Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics ( IBGE). To analyze data behavior over time, other indicators were constructed using other sources, e.g., Live Birth Information System (SINASC) and Cancer Information System (SISCAN). DATASUS databases are consolidated over time, varying according to the data system consulted, and permit receipt of new information or corrections during a time period. All indicators were recalculated for the period 2016 to 2022, including 2015 baseline. Calculated as: No. procedures in selected health services linked to the location of occurrence according to regional design of RN Health/Total no. selected procedures state-wide x 100 in period of one year.

title.narrative: Proportion of biopsies done after mammography

comment.narrative:
Achieved 18.2% Exam seeks early detection of breast cancer. Indicator is associated with renovated Oncology Centers (CROs) in the territory. Data is SISCAN. Calculated as: No. biopsies conducted after mammography in women 50-69 years/No. Mammography exams in women x 100. Numerator: Biopsy/excised breast nodule; anatomo-pathology exam of breast biopsy//Denominator: Bilateral mammography for screening.
Recalculated ranges: Baseline 2016, 2017 no change; 2018 = 0.35//2019 = 1.12//2020 = 0.59//2021 = 1.08//2022 = 0.77

title.narrative: Percentage of priority macroprocesses refurbished in the priority Government Institutions of the Project.

comment.narrative:
Achieved 167% of target.
Target was 60%, achieved 100%. Indicator monitored implementation of revised/improved/refurbished macro-processes in priority project entities (Health, Education, Public Security, Planning and Administration, State Controller's Office, State Attorney General. The 52 specific macro-processes prioritized and mapped in six agencies are listed in ICR Annex 7.

title.narrative: Number of people in rural areas provided with access to Improved Water Sources under the project

comment.narrative: Exceeded: Achieved 103.5% Improved water sources includes piped connections to households (connections within the house or on the patio), public sources (water fountains), perforated/drilled wells, excavated and protected wells, water source protection, and rainwater collection. Starting from the number of beneficiary families with structural investments and subprojects in water supply - Edital 1/2014 - the number of persons was estimated considering an average 3.4 residents per HH in rural areas (IBGE Census data). The result calculates subprojects financed and finalized (completed). The BCR shows a related sub-indicator "Number of subprojects in rural areas which obtained access to improved water sources under the Project". The reported result is 113 with a target of 150. However, Bank ISRs do not include/Measure such an indicator, and it is not mentioned in the PAD or Restructuring Papers.

title.narrative: Tourism and Cultural Infrastructure created / improved by the project

comment.narrative: Exceeded: Achieved 112.5% of target This indicator was introduced by the 2nd Restructuring (May 2019). The key tourism infrastructure renovated, rehabilitated or constructed with project suport was as follows: Teatro Alberto Maranhao (TAM); Escola de Danca do Teatro Alberto Maranhao (EDTAM); Biblioteca Camara Cascudo; Fortaleza dos Reis Magos; Memorial Camara Cascudo; Museu Cafe Filho; Palacio do Governo (Pinacoteca); Sinalizacao Turistica (ST - tourist signage) Polo Agreste/Trairi; Teatro Adjunto Dias; Teatro Lauro Monte Filho; Sistema de Esgotamento Sanitario do Sao Miguel de Gostoso; Sistema de Esgotamento Sanitario de Cerro-Cora; RN 160 (access to Airport); RN 063 (access to Barra de Tabatinga-Barreta suburb); RN 307 (Genipabu); Estrada Zona Industrial-Aeroporto; RN 087 - Lagoa Nova-Cerro-Cora; Sinalizacao Turistica (tourist signage) Polo Costa Branca; ST Polo Serido; ST Polo Serrano.

title.narrative: Reference center for the early detection of cancer, renovated, equipped and operational.

comment.narrative: Achieved 100%. Indicator is associated with activities in the Oncology Network. Referral centers for early detection were implemented, linked to public labs for diagnostic support and cancer treatment. "Operational" means quality attention to target pop. and reduced time between the diagnosis - early detection - and start of treatment. Calculated on number Referral Centers renovated, equipped and operational.

title.narrative: Extension of State roads improved by the project

comment.narrative:
Exceeded: Achieved 137% of target
Measures the number of cumulative kilometers of roads re-opened to motorized traffic - rehabilitated or modernized - by the Project. Roads involved: RN 307 (9 km); RN 063 (9 km); RN 087 (22 km); RN 160 (17 km); BR-437-RN 015 (19 km); RN 011 (31 km); RN 118 (47.5 km); RN 016 (57 km); Estrada da Producao (22 km); and RN 233 (41 km).

title.narrative: Productive and socio-environmental investment organizations/groups led by women

comment.narrative: Exceeded: Achieved 134.3% of target The PAD indicator was re-worded, changing "Group productive investments led by women" to "Group socio-environmental investments led by women" (ie. PSA subprojects). The wording was subsequently revised again to "Productive and Socio-environmental investment organizations/groups led by women" meaning both PINS (including PES) and PSA investments, the main types under Productive Inclusion.

title.narrative: Number of secretariats with second level contracting

comment.narrative:
Achieved 100% of target.
Indicator was introduced by the 1st Restructuring (June 2017) with target of 5 secretariats. Indicator pertained to secretariats which came under (require) Management Contracts (MC) via Decree #26.090 of May 17,2016 which controls Management Contracts through the State Executive. Target was to establish MCs in 5 state entities (and associated with the Project): SEPLAN, SEARH, SEEC, SESAP, SESED. In practice, almost all state entities came under MCs. MCs are no longer required, substituted by entities committing to specific actions specified in the State's Plano Plurianual.

title.narrative: Percentage of critical audit recommendations implemented

comment.narrative:
Achieved 118% of target. Target 50%, achieved 59%.
Indicator was intended to verify the percentage execution of the plan for implementation of state audit recommendations suggested in the Action Plan for Products 3 and 7 of the Auditoria Interna da Folha de Pagamento (State payroll) do Estado do RN. Products 3 and 7 were found by auditors to have inconsistencies in processes/contracts. Calculated by computing auditor recommendations in Reports 3 and 7. Auditors recommended 38 points to be adopted by State to eliminate situations of non-conformity/ineligible payments, plus more than 120 recommendations to improve controls, processes, systems and efficiency in processing the RN State Payroll.

title.narrative: Hospital Emergency rooms renovated, equipped, and concluded by the project.

comment.narrative: Achieved 71% of target. Indicator is associated with Urgency/Emergency services activities financed. Emergency rooms were renovated in five principal hospitals in respective regions, and two ERs are still under completion in two other regions. Renovations were designed to improve these units' capacity to resolve health emergencies and reduce attendance response time. The target was originally 4, increased to 5, then 7, including the Acu Hospital. Measurement is the number of facilities renovated and/or equipped by the Project. Facilities renovated or under completion: HR Monsenhor Antonio Barros; HR Lindolfo Gomes Vidal, HR Josefa Alves Godeiro, HR do Serido-Telecila F. Fontes, HR Monsenhor Expedito S de Medeiros, HR Cleodon C. de Andrade, and HR Nelson Inacio dos Santos.

title.narrative: Schools with computer labs with adequate use

comment.narrative: Achieved 108.6% of target. Designed to evaluate adequate use of computer labs in schools, devise a pedagogical strategy for their use, and having teachers use the lab weekly for instruction of students. Lab was adequately used if: (i) possessed a technology teaching/instruction plan; (ii) 80% of teachers able to use software, apps and technologies; (iii) at least 3 disciplines had weekly classes in the computer lab. Calculated as: # schools with adequate use of informatics lab/# schools with informatics labs financed by the Project. Schools that receive computer labs financed by the project and use them appropriately - there is a pedagogical strategy for it, teachers have been trained and are using it weekly.

title.narrative: Regularized properties surveyed and registered in the Computerized System

comment.narrative:
Achieved 108.6% of target. Target 70%, achieved 76%.
This indicator, introduced in 2017, monitored the percentage of properties surveyed and registered in the State Information System (SIAF, then SIGEF). Survey of the State's Public Administration property assets would identify properties needing regularization of title and to insert cadastral information on the properties inventoried, as well as documents digitized in the Integrated System of Assets Management. Of an estimated 3,449 properties, 61% were not regularized. Results were calculated when a building/property had been approved legally, along with its engineering, then registered in the system. At the final execution of the Contract (signed for these services), some 76% of identified properties had been regularized.

title.narrative: Schools of Pedagogical Innovation Projects (PIP) that have satisfactorily implemented subprojects.

comment.narrative: Achieved 93.3% of target Measured based on ratio between the number of schools considered satisfactory and the total schools accounted for in the PIP. Concept of satisfactory is attributed to each school at end of school year based on following criteria: (i) execution of at least 80% of financial resources transferred; (ii) received all programming visits; (iii) school has executed at least 80% of activities established in its Action Plan.

title.narrative: Guidelines and curricular matrices disseminated in state schools

comment.narrative:
Achieved 148.3%
Main source of data: Mobilization Report, which were the instruments provided by and resulting from discussions of the matrices in each State school throughout the period when this document was being prepared. Guidelines and Curricular Matrices would be considered disseminated in schools when 80% of State schools participating in the workshops had presented their Mobilization Reports.

title.narrative: Community organizations with fee collection arrangements for the management and maintenance of the water supply subprojects financed by the project.

comment.narrative: Exceeded: Achieved 119% of target This indicator measures the sustainability of the Project's water supply investments. Those considered are the water supply subprojects resulting from Edital 1/2014. The calculation includes subprojects financed and finalized from Edital 1/2014 with investments concluded and with six months of full operation. Each beneficiary community organization was canvassed to verify whether they had an arrangement for the management and maintenance of their water supply system. The full history of these investments is described in the BCR.

title.narrative: Proportion of women whose births were performed in the region where they live, in relation to the total number of births performed in the state.

comment.narrative: Not achieved: The baseline was 72.48%, the target was 85% and the Project achieved 67.11 %, equal to - 43% of the expected 12.5 percentage point increase. Indicator is associated with activities within the maternal/infant health network, and reflects lack of completion and/or operationalization (professional staffing) of project facilities at the closing date. Formula: # admittances for labor/childbirth of residents attended in own area of residence/total admittances for labor/childbirth of residents state-wide. Note that increase continued at 2% per year up to 2019. All indicators recalculated for study period 2016-2023 incl. 2015 baseline.

title.narrative: Productive investments supported by the project adopting sustainable social, crop production, and/or environmental practices

comment.narrative:
Exceeded: Achieved 180% of target This indicator measures the number of producer beneficiaries with productive subprojects who adopted sustainable social, agricultural production or environmental practices recommended by the Project. The agreements signed with the respective organizations were the basis for establishing parameters for calculation and to verify the achievement as a percentage.
Method: Number of producer organizations benefited with productive subprojects and adopting the practices mentioned above, divided by the number of producer organizations benefited with productive subprojects (119) X 100.

title.narrative: Productive Investiments for market access with sanitary compliance

comment.narrative: Achieved 125.5% of target. This indicator was introduced by the 1st restructuring in June 2017 with target of 100. Target was reduced to 60 by 2nd restructuring in May 2019 because the overall target for SPs financed was reduced due to protracted drought and delayed start-up of investments. There were 119 productive SPs of which 74 were subject to sanitary certification and were certified. Applying the baseline of 5, the final result is an achievement of 69 over baseline or 125.5%.
